newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks close higher, focus on property.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks close higher, focus on property.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended higher on Thursday, with the market focus seen on small-capitalised property counters due to speculative reasons, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index rose 1.53 points, or 0.24 percent, to close at 652.98 points after touching a day low of 648.87 points.
Advancers led decliners by 72 to 61 with 54 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 430 billion rupiah compared with 433 billion rupiah on Wednesday.
"A spurt of late buying particularly in some big-caps and active local buying of second-liners helped the index to close higher after being in negative territory most of the day," one broker said.
Brokers said local players appeared to take an increasing role in driving the market as could be seen from the large number of small stocks traded in the past few days.

"The reasons for the buying may not be clear, but many local players just do not care. Seeing that prices could rise by 25 rupiah or 50 rupiah would be enough to attract their interest," another broker said.
Brokers said property firm Elang Realty, which rose another 150 rupiah to close at 1,300 rupiah, was traded in huge volumes for the fourth consecutive day mostly by local players.
Some 56 million Elang shares were traded on Thursday compared with 55 million on Wednesday and 38 million on Tuesday on rumours the firm was expected to announce a rights issue, brokers said.
Another small property firm Suryamas was also actively traded, with 31 million shares changing hands largely for speculative reasons, brokers said.
Other small property firms Pudjiadi and Mas Murni were actively traded also on speculation, brokers said.
Big-cap Telkom rose 25 rupiah to 3,650 rupiah following the firm's announcement late on Wednesday that it would pay a dividend of 41.25 rupiah for 1996.
